compareCandidate.label: Jupiter's Great Red Spot vs. Earth's hurricanes
compareCandidate.description: The Great Red Spot is a storm — the same kind of whirling weather system as an Earth hurricane, but about as wide as our whole planet and raging for at least 190 years. Comparing the two shows that 'weather' is a universal phenomenon, just on wildly different scales.

processes: Volcanoes built over billions of years without plate tectonics
Canyons formed by rifting and erosion
plainLanguageExplanation: Every world has a famous feature, and each one teaches a different idea. Jupiter's Great Red Spot is the biggest storm in the solar system — a swirling hurricane more than twice as wide as Earth that has been spinning for at least 190 years. Mars has Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano known anywhere — about 22 km high, nearly three Mount Everests — and Valles Marineris, a canyon system so long it would stretch across the whole United States. Saturn's rings look solid in photos but are actually trillions of separate chunks of ice and rock, some the size of houses. Earth's oceans and continents are the features we live on — the only world in the solar system with liquid water on its surface. And the Moon's dark patches, the maria, are ancient plains of lava that flooded after giant impacts. This model shows each world with its landmarks highlighted by hotspots, so you can explore the solar system's geography like a world-traveler.

whyItMatters: These landmarks are the reasons we send missions: the Great Red Spot teaches storm dynamics, Olympus Mons teaches volcanic building without plate tectonics, Valles Marineris teaches the history of Martian water and rifting, and the Moon's maria record the bombardment the young solar system went through. Every one of these features is a page in the solar system's history book — and some, like Earth's oceans, raise the question no other world answers: where is the water, and where is the life?
didYouKnow: Valles Marineris is so long that it would stretch across the entire United States — and its deepest point is about seven times deeper than the Grand Canyon.
